entries.test: Dated public investigations and documented disinformation operations would establish how quickly bad actors adopted LLMs to generate disinformation.
entries.note: The proposition captures one independently asserted part of the sentence.

entries.test: Documented coordinated AI bot operations and comparative evidence of their reach, deception, and persuasive effects would test whether they present a greater disinformation threat than earlier bots.
entries.note: “We foresee” expresses a firm expectation without a deadline.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and independent detection studies would test whether existing swarms coordinate synthetic personas whose collective behavior is difficult to distinguish from human communities.
entries.note: “Can” asserts a present capability, rather than merely a possible future outcome.

entries.test: Published experiments or documented operations would test whether swarms infiltrate communities, gain credibility, and adjust messages in real time using audience responses.
entries.note: The sentence asserts capabilities; the drafter’s “could” label does not determine checkability.

entries.test: Public network analyses and controlled experiments would test whether thousands of personas controlled by one operator replace independent contributions with coordinated signals.
entries.note: The surrounding text gives “independence” a concrete meaning: distinct contributors rather than one operator’s masks.

entries.test: Public investment records and Doublespeed’s advertised and demonstrated capabilities would establish whether venture funding supports industrial-scale astroturfing and whether that activity is AI-driven.
entries.note: The author endorses the funding and industrialization claim, but the cited passage does not establish that Doublespeed’s astroturfing is AI-driven.

entries.test: Controlled studies measuring perceived majority opinion before and after exposure to fabricated swarm activity would test the proposed social-evidence mechanism.
entries.note: This is a testable causal capability claim.

entries.test: Published data-poisoning experiments tracing swarm-generated crawler-targeted content into training datasets and subsequent model behavior would test the claimed mechanism.
entries.note: The proposition drops “duplicative” from the stated antecedent. The passage describes a causal capability, not a firm prediction that poisoning will occur.

entries.test: Public experiments exposing reasoning models to training-data poisoning would establish whether those models are vulnerable to the described manipulation.
entries.note: “This” refers back to the preceding description of LLM grooming.

entries.test: Public evaluations of bans and anti-swarm interventions would test whether bans alone eliminate the threat and whether interventions change attackers’ costs.
entries.note: The claim concerns the effectiveness of interventions, making causal the better classification.
The rest of the paragraph explicitly supplies continuous monitoring as the recommended replacement.

entries.test: Detection benchmarks comparing copy-matching methods against AI-generated campaigns with unique posts would test the claimed loss of effectiveness.
entries.note: The plain contextual target is detecting the described AI swarms.
The record combines a recommendation with a firm prediction of reactive defenses failing. The prediction could be screened separately; the combined recommendation is normative.
This recommends a policy and states its intended purpose.

entries.test: Public implementation results and adversarial audits of anonymous proof-of-human requirements would establish the technical difficulty and financial cost of secretly operating ten thousand accounts.
entries.note: The normalization weakens “mathematically difficult” to generic difficulty and leaves “financially ruinous” less explicit. The forecast has a stated antecedent but no deadline.
“Vetted researchers” broadens the specified beneficiaries beyond academic and civil society researchers. Existing access restrictions are a separately checkable factual premise.
The detection mandate is explicit in the following sentences of the same paragraph.

entries.test: Public measurements of swarm deployment costs, identity fabrication time, and successful manipulation attempts would test whether cheap, rapid fabrication enables attacks on public discourse.
entries.note: The source specifies monetary cost for coordinating a mob and elapsed time for fabricating an identity. The proposition turns both into a monetary claim.

entries.test: Public records of bot-swarm operations available by January 2026, including deployment costs, detection, attribution, and penalties, would test whether large swarms could be launched cheaply with little risk.
entries.note: The publication date appropriately anchors “right now”; “can” asserts an existing capability.
